chapter: Arranging for other bandleaders and closing talk
title: How Millinder wanted his arrangements specified
summary: He left arranging to Horace's judgment but named soloists to feature and paid for the charts.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Uh-huh. That's great. Really great. What -- did you have any special sort of things in arranging for him or just --

No. No, he left it to your judgment. He wanted you to naturally, like invite other guys, to hear his band, and he wanted you to -- oh, he would specify to give certain solos to certain guys. I don't know if they were his pets or not, but most of his trumpet players could play the part, you know. But I think he favored -- you know, had his favorites, so he would tell you to give so and so the solo on you know -- whether this, and that, so -- but he was impressing me, you know, as to what he wanted, where there was just -- of course, he paid for the arrangements, so that was his privilege.
